$comment: Single source of truth for the Luxar gallery harness. Consumed by BOTH scripts/gallery/generate_gallery_datasets.py (dataset generation) and packages/luxar-viewer/src/tests/screenshots/generate-gallery.spec.ts (still + orbit-video capture). Add a demo here to include it in the gallery; nothing else needs updating. The authoritative field list is the DemoEntry interface in generate-gallery.spec.ts; this comment and scripts/gallery/README.md must be kept in step with it. REQUIRED: id (gallery media filename stem; must equal the demo key), title (caption), geometry, category, script (demo_*.py under packages/luxar/src/luxar/demos, or null if the demo lives only on a feature branch and its dataset must be pre-generated; currently unused), dataset (authoritative store path under datasets/demos, relative to repo root). OPTIONAL: citation (dataset credit, copied verbatim from the demo's DEMO_META["citation"]["short"] and pinned equal to it by test_demo_meta.py; present only for a demo that declares a real credit — an absent key means 'unknown or not yet recorded', which is NOT the same claim as 'nothing to credit'; the capture code never reads it), exposure (log2-stops override; omit for auto-exposure), autoFrame (default true; set false for very heavy scenes to skip fill-to-screen and use the baked camera), autoExpose (default true; set false to use the demo's baked exposure), fillTarget (per-demo screen-coverage target for fill-to-screen; default 0.95), zoom (multiplicative zoom after fill: >1 in, <1 out), distance (absolute camera distance in world units — bypasses fill; for faint/diffuse subjects), viewAngle ({azimuth, elevation} in degrees — orients the camera before framing), orbitUp ('x'|'y'|'z' world up-axis the rock revolves about; DEFAULT = derived from the camera's own up-vector, so a baked non-Y up is honoured automatically - set this only to override, and note it also re-parks the camera on that axis and so usually wants a viewAngle beside it), dimensionNav ({key, steps} for nD demos), timelapse ({framePoint} — advance the time dim while recording a 4D series; framePoint = fraction of the range used to frame the still), lodFinest (default true; set false for a very heavy scene so the coverage-based LOD may pick a lighter level), note (free-text human annotation; the capture code never reads it).

demos.title: Cryo-EM Giant Virus Capsid
demos.note: FILLTARGET: the default 0.95 framed this as an edge-to-edge texture wall — you could not tell it was a capsid. Measured border-lit across the pose set, 10/10 poses flagged at every step: 70.6% at 0.95, 34.2% at 0.85, 17.7% at 0.75, 15.2% at 0.65. The harness keeps suggesting lower because a dense icosahedron inherently clips its own silhouette, so 0.65 was chosen on the RENDER, not on the warning clearing: at 0.65 the hexagonal outline, the capsomer texture and the tail stalk are all legible. Auto-exposure tracks the framing and is the other half of the fix — -1.06 stops at 0.95 (subject filled the frame, so the meter crushed it to muddy brown) vs +2.33 at 0.65. Coverage cannot see any of this: it read 93% at 0.95 and 63% at 0.65, i.e. it preferred the broken framing, because its percentile bbox ignores exactly these outliers. This is a FRAMING fault, not the fit: at 19.2 dB foreground PSNR it is among the four lowest-scoring hosted archives, but opencell_map4 renders well at 18.0 dB, so the metric was never what made this tile look bad. STALE FIGURES: both dB numbers predate #1914 (2026-08-23), which fixed five call sites that scored a fit against the raw volume when a fit reconstructs V minus image_min. These two figures therefore use the wrong basis in an unpredictable direction. The framing conclusion above is unaffected — it never rested on the metric.

demos.title: Cells3D Isosurfaces
demos.citation: Allen Institute for Cell Science (scikit-image cells3d)
demos.note: the first SHADED tile. EXPOSURE: the offset-key capture's frame 0 measures p10 0.378, p50 0.506, p99 0.597, spread 0.219 over 32,845 lit pixels. The p50 landing on TARGET_MID confirms the auto-exposure flat-subject pass still fired under the wider asymmetric lighting distribution. This tile deliberately carries NO exposure override because the policy already puts its median on target; the final-frame spread is an outcome measurement, not the post-phase-1 gate input used to calibrate NARROW_SPREAD_MAX. ORBITUP+VIEWANGLE: the orbit hard-sets cam.up to the orbitUp axis, and the default WAS world-y at the time, which silently discarded this demo's baked up=(1,0,0) - the shipped animation was rolled ~90deg away from its own poster AND tumbled, subject aspect swinging 0.40..0.92 (130pct) over one rock. orbitUp x matches the baked up and makes the rock a real turntable, but positionForOrbitUp then parks the camera edge-on to this thin slab (aspect ~4.5, lit fraction 0.09, a sliver), so viewAngle 45/40 is REQUIRED alongside it, not optional; together they hold aspect at 1.46..1.50 (2.5pct swing). The default now derives from the camera's own up-vector and would reach x unaided, but orbitUp x is retained deliberately because it also triggers positionForOrbitUp, and the viewAngle 45/40 is calibrated against that parked pose. FILLTARGET: the fill loop closes on an OUTLIER-ROBUST percentile bbox, but what reaches the frame edge is exactly the outliers - detached membrane specks and the slab's far corners - so the robust metric reports a fit while the true extent is cropped. Measured over EVERY orbit frame (the README embeds the animation, not the still), border-lit pixels: 0.84 -> 3389, 0.75 -> 1256, 0.69 -> 0 across all 120 frames. Captured on an NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000; a macOS/Metal run reproduced the same three numbers within 1pct

demos.note: fillTarget 0.65: before #2176, at the default 0.95 the globe was cropped past its own limb and read as a noise wall rather than as Earth — 3658/4316 border pixels (84.8%) lit. The value was originally derived against that 2M-point stippled shell and CARRIED OVER CORRECTLY when #2176 rebuilt the globe as a textured UV-sphere mesh: re-measured after that change at 0.0% border-lit and 72% coverage. The committed README tile predates the rebuild, so those post-mesh figures describe the current demo rather than the checked-in media. Worth keeping because the mesh limb is both harder-edged and brighter (the cloud shell is luminous on a slightly larger sphere, so the rim gains luminance seen edge-on), which pushes border-lit up at framing that is actually correct — judge this tile on the render, not the metric.

demos.title: Nuclear Pore Complex
demos.note: fillTarget 0.70, re-derived after #2262 replaced one Nup107-160 Y-complex ring (41,288 elements) with the whole pore (9,874,128) — a 239x change, so the previous 0.75 was metered on a different object. Three arms, final coverage / final lit / border-lit: 0.75 -> 85.8% / 73.9% / 504 of 4316 (11.7%); 0.70 -> 77.8% / 62.3% / 70 (1.6%); 0.65 -> 71.3% / 53.1% / 1 (0.0%). CHOSEN ON THE RENDER, not on the warning clearing. The still is well framed at ALL THREE values — the crop metric spans all 10 orbit poses, so a clean still can carry a real warning from a pose nobody sees in isolation. Pulling orbit frames with ffmpeg settled it: at 0.75 the outer lilac ring is cut flat against the frame edge, at 0.70 every frame is complete with margin. 0.65 removes the last graze but shrinks the subject visibly for no gain the eye can see. Note the harness suggested 0.65 -> 0.55 for a SINGLE lit pixel: it recommends lower whenever a dense silhouette grazes an edge, which a rotating disc always eventually will, so do not follow it mechanically.

demos.title: Exotic Mathematical Surfaces
demos.note: The 3x3 grid is a flat WALL (~3.6 x 3.6 x 1.0), so viewAngle is deliberately omitted: an oblique view collapses the nine cells into one mass. fillTarget 0.72 was measured with additive transport; 0.62 keeps the wall safely framed with both additive and volumetric layers. There is also a hidden two-stop categorical `family` axis that swaps the entire wall (0 = triply-periodic minimal surfaces, 1 = algebraic); this tile shows family 0, which reads as the more coherent grid. A second tile could show family 1 via dimensionNav.

demos.citation: Barry 2021 (GIANI, Zenodo 5270323); Cell Tracking Challenge (Maška et al. 2023)
demos.note: the old volumetric white-out was fixed by coupling strong absorption (kappa 3.13) with low opacity (0.06); the scene bakes exposure=1.97 and a 0-1.085 display window, so auto-exposure recalibrates. The faint bg rectangle is gone as of the floor fix: the fit now subtracts the specimen's ~675-count haze, not just the ~205-count detector offset, removing ~84% of the scene's emitted mass while leaving nuclei brightness ~unchanged. fillTarget 0.7 gives the elongated embryo a correctly filled poster frame; border-lit only falls from 54.9% to 48.4% because the subject projects wider at rock +15deg. The harness's suggested 0.6 would shrink the still to optimize the worst orbit pose instead.

demos.title: 4D Zebrafish Gastrulation (endoderm)
demos.note: framePoint 0.9 because the specimen migrates and grows: the labelled endoderm is ~2–4 cells at t=0 and ~185 by t=300 min, while the scene bounds are the acquisition cage (859 × 859 × 316 µm), not the specimen. A bounds-based auto-fit at frame 0 therefore frames an almost-empty box with a dot in it — correct by every metric and useless as a tile. 0.9 rather than 1.0 keeps structure legible while the endoderm has spread across the yolk. fillTarget is deliberately left at the cage-based default: the cage IS the scale reference for a 2%-occupancy specimen, so cropping to the specimen would lose the idea.

demos.title: Splat Culling Study (Drosophila gastrulation)
demos.note: Ten cumulative-amplitude cull levels of one Drosophila gastrulation fit stacked on a categorical Cull selector. The tile deliberately shows the DEFAULT slice, which is the uncut level: the demo's point is the comparison you make by stepping the selector, and any single culled level would misrepresent it as a picture of damage. No dimensionNav for the same reason — it only positions a still. The generic timelapse sweep was considered but rejected because its warm-up starts this 0–9 range at index 1, omitting the uncut reference level from the video.

demos.title: 4D Drosophila Embryogenesis (500 timepoints)
demos.note: fillTarget 0.80, not the 0.9 inherited from the h2afva timelapse: this embryo is a ~2.5:1 prolate ellipsoid, so at 0.9 it is cut flat at BOTH poles — and for an embryogenesis timelapse the anterior/posterior ends are the subject, not spare margin. Border-lit fell 737/4316 (17.1%) to 16/4316 (0.4%), a 46x reduction, and the render shows the whole embryo with margin at 0.80. The harness then suggested 0.7 for those 16 remaining pixels; that is its standing over-suggestion on any subject whose silhouette grazes an edge and was not followed. framePoint 0.9 KEPT: late in the 500-timepoint series the nuclei are individually resolved and the ventral furrow is legible, which is the point of the demo. Store needs no LOD work — the hosted archive is already flat with 14 additive rungs and no substitutive levels. Its largest node reads 37,930,613 (9x the 4,194,304 floor) but Time is display=false over [0.0, 249.5] step 0.5, so the resident slice is 166,443, i.e. 25x UNDER; this is the store _lod_policy.py cites for exactly that point.

demos.title: Bird Plumage Colour Space (ultraviolet 4th axis)
demos.citation: BirdColorBase (Gluckman & Endler, and ten contributing groups)
demos.note: TIMELAPSE, not dimensionNav: the hidden axis is UV chroma (10 deciles), and timelapse resolves the FIRST non-displayed dim, which here is unambiguously it. The traverse IS the finding - decile 1 is a yellow/orange carotenoid spray, decile 10 is almost entirely structural blues and violets. framePoint 0.95 frames the still on decile 10, chosen by measurement rather than taste: per-decile chroma-weighted hue-sector occupancy and mean chroma are 3 sectors / 28.8 at decile 1, falling to 5 sectors / 5.2 at decile 9, then rising to 6 sectors / 10.0 at decile 10. So the conventional 0.85 would land on decile 9 - the SHORTEST spikes of all ten and a stubby frame - while decile 10 has both the widest hue coverage and long spikes, because that bin spans 24.2-74.8% UV and catches the strongly structural colours. THE CROP WARNING ON THIS TILE IS EXPECTED OUTPUT, NOT A DEFECT: chroma is violently right-skewed (median 8.4, p99 63.8, max 117.9), so framing the true extent puts the whole corpus in the middle fifth of the frame. fillTarget 0.8 frames the p99.5 chroma quantile (70.8) and roughly 1,800 spikes overshoot the frame edge BY DESIGN. Do not tighten fillTarget to drive border-lit pixels to zero - border contact here is composition. No viewAngle: the baked pose (distance 267.7 CIELAB units, 16.3 deg elevation, 24.2 deg off the L* axis) is deliberate - looking straight down L* collapses the hedgehog into a flat rainbow star and hides the third axis, tilting further stops the hue circle reading as a circle. Judge exposure on whether the SHORT central spikes keep their hue, not on overall brightness: additive blending over 360,432 readings makes the neutral core bright on purpose, and opacity 0.33 / intensity 0.40 were tuned against exactly that after 0.55/0.55 turned the core into a flat white wedge
